display.purpose: Game title (banner section) and shift-end score reveals. Max two instances per screen.

body.purpose: Commands, descriptions, chat messages. All gameplay instruction text.

narrative.overview:
This is a cooking game played in a dungeon — specifically, the kind of warm, earthy, survival-cooking dungeon that Dungeon Meshi depicts. The visual language lives at the intersection of a torch-lit adventurer's camp kitchen and a Jackbox party screen: dark cave stone behind everything, warm fire-orange commanding every action, parchment-colored text that reads from across a Twitch stream on a phone.

The palette draws from dungeon ecology: dark warm stone, amber torch fire, earthy monster herb greens, alchemical purple. These are not decorative choices — they map to game states. Torch-orange is action and heat. Verdure green is success. Signal red is danger. Dungeon gold is reward.

This system rejects four failure modes: SaaS dashboard, streaming overlay, cute kawaii, and fantasy RPG title screen.
keyCharacteristics: Dark warm dungeon stone as the base layer; all surfaces warm-tinted, never cold grey
Broadcast-first scale: 18px minimum for all text, key game elements 22-56px
Full palette: torch-flame (primary action), verdure (success), arcane (magic/adventure), dungeon-gold (reward)
Tactile press physics on buttons: hard bottom shadow that collapses on active
Order tickets as physical parchment artifacts with perforated edges
CSS custom property family (--accent, --accent-secondary, --accent-tertiary, --accent-gold) for all accent colors

rules.name: The Dungeon Fire Rule
rules.body: Torch Flame (var(--accent)) is the sole primary action color. One fire color, one meaning.

rules.name: The Warm Stone Rule
rules.body: Every neutral surface is tinted toward amber. Cold grey is prohibited.

rules.name: The Gold Scarcity Rule
rules.body: Dungeon Gold (var(--accent-gold)) appears only on money values and reward feedback. Not decorative.

rules.name: The Broadcast Scale Rule
rules.body: Base font size is var(--base-fs) = 18px (24px on mobile). Non-negotiable.

rules.name: The Flat Surface Rule
rules.body: No ambient box-shadow on static containers. Tonal contrast handles depth. Shadows for button press and overlays only.

dos: Do use var(--accent) for every primary interactive action.
Do size all visible text at var(--base-fs) = 18px minimum.
Do apply tactile press shadow (0 4px 0 var(--accent-deep)) on primary buttons.
Do treat order tickets as physical parchment: perforated tears, punch holes, aged paper.
Do use tonal contrast for surface elevation — shadows for overlays and button press only.
Do use the CSS custom property family (var(--accent) etc.) rather than hardcoding hex.
Do keep broadcast scale in mind: readable on a 375px phone watching a stream.
donts: Don't use #ffffff or #000000. Cave Dark is the floor; Parchment is the ceiling.
Don't make it look like a SaaS dashboard: no white cards, no muted blue CTAs.
Don't make it look like a streaming overlay: no neon on black, no OBS widgets.
Don't make it cute or pastel. The kitchen has weight.
Don't add fantasy RPG title screen aesthetics: no dark purple auras, no gothic darkness.
Don't use border-left stripes as status accents.
Don't use Dungeon Gold decoratively — money and rewards only.
Don't use Twitch Purple outside Twitch integration surfaces.
